# Job Chapter 32 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 428r–428v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_032_page_001.jpg, JOB_032_page_002.jpg

---

**1** At this point, the three friends stopped answering Job, because he remained convinced of his own innocence.

**2** Then Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite, from the clan of Ram, became furious. He was angry at Job for claiming to be right and God wrong.

**3** He was also angry at the three friends because they had failed to answer Job, even though they had condemned him.

**4** Now Elihu had held back from speaking because the others were all older than he was.

**5** But when Elihu realized that the three friends had nothing more to say, his anger boiled over.

**6** So Elihu son of Barakel the Buzite spoke up: "I am young, and you are old; that is why I held back and was afraid to share my thoughts with you.

**7** I thought, 'Those who are older should speak first; those with many years should teach what wisdom is.'

**8** But in reality, it is the spirit God puts in a person — the breath of the Almighty — that gives understanding.

**9** Age alone does not make someone wise; being old does not guarantee good judgment.

**10** So I say: listen to me! Let me tell you what I think.

**11** Look — I waited while you spoke. I listened carefully to your reasoning while you searched for the right words.

**12** I paid close attention, and not one of you proved Job wrong. Not one of you answered his arguments.

**13** Don't say, 'We have found true wisdom — only God can refute him, not us.'

**14** Now, Job has not directed his arguments at me, so I will not answer him with your same tired responses.

**15** The three of you are baffled — you have run out of things to say; words have completely failed you.

**16** Should I keep waiting just because you have stopped talking? Just because you stand there with nothing left?

**17** No — I will have my say. I will share what I know.

**18** I am bursting with words! The spirit inside me is pressing me to speak.

**19** My insides are like a sealed wineskin filled with fermenting wine — ready to explode like new wineskins about to burst!

**20** I have to speak so I can breathe again; I must open my mouth and give my answer.

**21** I will not take sides or flatter anyone.

**22** I don't know how to flatter — and if I did, my Maker would quickly put an end to me."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The unexpected newcomer:** Elihu appears out of nowhere — never mentioned before, never mentioned after. His detailed genealogy (the only one in the dialogues) feels like an overcompensation for his lack of introduction. The narrator tells us he is angry four times in five verses — a rhetorical signal that the reader should pay attention but perhaps also be cautious.

**v.8 — The spirit gives understanding:** Elihu's most important theological contribution: wisdom does not come from age but from God's spirit. This is genuinely insightful — and it challenges the entire assumption of the wisdom tradition that experience equals understanding.

**v.19 — About to burst:** Elihu compares himself to a wineskin full of fermenting wine. The image is vivid, energetic, and — let's be honest — a little self-important. Elihu is so full of himself that he might literally pop. The author may be inviting the reader to smile.

**The structural role of Elihu:** Elihu serves as a bridge between Job's final speech and God's appearance in the whirlwind. Whether his speeches are a later addition or part of the original design is one of the great questions in Job scholarship. Either way, he delays the divine response — and delay is its own kind of suffering.

*— PNEUMA*
